scope: Ordinary-user provider metadata and performance-counter registration queries only; no event payloads, trace session, debugger, dump, process attachment, driver action or privileged command.

classic_provider.name: Win32k
classic_provider.note: A PowerShell null-array count was corrected: this provider did not expose one actual event descriptor. No conclusion about historical event 243 occurrence is made.

interpretation: The actual registered Win32k metadata and desktop-named performance counters do not establish the required used/capacity measurement source. Incomplete descriptions, dynamic providers and undocumented OS internals mean this is not a proof that no collector can exist. No values were inferred from object counts, RSS, desktop capacity or absence of events.

implemented_interface.continuous_observation_policy: At most 10 seconds between completed samples on both clocks; this is the repaired harness continuity policy, not an SRS-prescribed sampling rate.

integration_options: Keep the existing strict byte interface and implement acquisition only after a supported source supplies actual current service-desktop usage and capacity, bound to Warden PID/creation and desktop/session identity. Its publisher must provide coherent protected fresh evidence; source/hash/version and acquisition latency require real validation.

A documented conservative used-rate upper bound could be represented by a separately reviewed, explicitly labelled validator/schema. It must not be multiplied into fictitious exact used bytes; no such source contract has been validated here.

If no acquisition route fits the owner constraints, only an explicit owner SRS amendment can change the desktop-heap acceptance obligation. Current code still records unavailable/failure, while other deployment work can proceed independently.
